problem_text:
A city planner needs to distribute a fixed budget across 12 infrastructure projects to maximize the overall community benefit score.  
The characteristics of each project are as follows:  
* Project A: benefit score 0.082, environmental impact 0.141, allocation bounds [0.000, 0.487]  
* Project B: benefit score 0.198, environmental impact 0.071, allocation bounds [0.053, 0.362]  
* Project C: benefit score 0.181, environmental impact 0.234, allocation bounds [0.073, 0.602]  
* Project D: benefit score 0.198, environmental impact 0.177, allocation bounds [0.095, 0.484]  
* Project E: benefit score 0.046, environmental impact 0.056, allocation bounds [0.089, 0.339]  
* Project F: benefit score 0.175, environmental impact 0.238, allocation bounds [0.076, 0.327]  
* Project G: benefit score 0.052, environmental impact 0.236, allocation bounds [0.053, 0.869]  
* Project H: benefit score 0.035, environmental impact 0.048, allocation bounds [0.002, 0.574]  
* Project I: benefit score 0.080, environmental impact 0.136, allocation bounds [0.000, 0.612]  
* Project J: benefit score 0.198, environmental impact 0.135, allocation bounds [0.073, 0.614]  
* Project K: benefit score 0.076, environmental impact 0.134, allocation bounds [0.023, 0.560]  
* Project L: benefit score 0.030, environmental impact 0.148, allocation bounds [0.088, 0.712]  

Each project must receive a proportion of the total budget within its specified bounds, and the sum of all proportions must equal one.  
To ensure equitable regional development, the subset of projects in high-priority zones L = {A, B, C, E, F, G, I, J, L} must collectively receive at least 0.506 of the total budget.  
Additionally, the total environmental impact of all projects must not exceed 0.170, and the overall community benefit score must be at least 0.086.  
Determine the optimal budget allocation that maximizes the total community benefit while satisfying all constraints.
